compute.note: CONFLICT, parameters left null: VarBench's Hubbard/supplements/Imada_group_overview.md says "alpha = 1, full network", while sub_rbm_phidx.py generates a translation-invariant (1x1) RBM. The script's own architecture would have 66051 complex parameters (formula below), recorded here only. samples = NVMCSample x MPI processes / NSplitSize = 100 x 8 / 1 = 800 per SR step: with NSplitSize = 1 every rank is its own sampling group (vmcmain.c "group1 = rank0/NSplitSize"), draws NVMCSample samples after NVMCWarmUp = 100 (each separated by NVMCInterval x Nsite = 256 proposals) and WeightAverageWE sums the weights over all ranks (average.c); iterations = NSROptItrStep = 1000 SR steps (the parameters are averaged over the last NSROptItrSmp = 100). All of these are the defaults of make_modpara, not overridden by the optimisation call. Each amplitude sums a Pfaffian of the 214-electron pair-product state over NSPGaussLeg x |NMPTrans| = 8 x 256 = 2048 spin/momentum projection points. Doubt (why confidence is low): the script is the simplified template of programs/mVMC_makedef/README.txt ("For simplicity, we focus on the case of Ns=8x8"). It runs ONE optimisation stage with the projections and the RBM on from the start, while the README's protocol has three optimisation stages (f_ij alone from the UHF solution, then the RBM, then the projections) whose step counts are not stated anywhere, and it never runs the Lanczos step the energy includes: make_all.py also writes namelist_aft.def/modpara_aft.def (NVMCCalMode=1, NLanczosMode=1, NVMCWarmUp=500, NVMCInterval=5, NVMCSample=5000, NDataQtySmp=10) but mVMC.sh does not call it. So the counts are the script's single stage, not the published run's total. No time is recorded anywhere; "mpiexec -np 8" names MPI processes, not hardware.

compute.reported_as: Sec. IV (Testing the method): The few parameter choice adopted in Ref. 54 is used only to initialize the present most general 8W + 1 (by including also the optimization of H_MF(alpha) and Delta tau) parameter ansatz |psi_tau>. || Sec. V: in order to compare the stripe with periodicity W = 8 and W = 7 and the uniform d-wave solution, calculations on a 16 x 16 and 14 x 16 clusters are carried out with 16 x 16 different twists in the BZ. || Sec. VI: For this reason for U/t = 2 (U/t = 4) a much larger mesh for the TABC was used with 64 x 64 (32 x 32) different twists in the BZ, instead of the smaller 16 x 16 grid used for U/t = 8 and U/t = 6. [...] much larger cluster simulations are prohibitive at present. || Fig. 11 caption: [...] at the lowest T_eff (i.e. largest tau t = 4, 2.6, 1.73, 1.3 for U/t = 2, 4, 6, 8, respectively) and 16 x 16 cluster. [...] In these calculations, in order to reduce at most the stochastic bias, at each iteration a quite large number (> 3 x 10^5) of samples for evaluating energy derivatives was used [...] || Sec. V (half filling): However, tau t <= 1.3 has been chosen also in this case, in order to show the strength of this approach even when short time projections are employed. || Acknowledgments: I acknowledge PRACE for awarding access to Marconi at CINECA Italy, and Riken collaboration for access to HOKUSAI supercomputer in Saitama Japan.

compute.note: parameters = 65 is the paper's formula for the most general stripe ansatz, 8W + 1 variational parameters, evaluated at the stated stripe width W = 8 (the number 65 itself is not printed; the formula is). Worklist row cites the journal URL (PRB 107, 115133, 2023) = arXiv:2101.07045 (S. Sorella, VAFQMC). No run time, core count, core-hours or per-run sample count is stated for any energy in the paper; the only sample statement (> 3 x 10^5 samples per optimisation iteration) is given for the uniform d-wave ansatz optimisation of Fig. 11 on 16 x 16, not for the stripe runs, so samples is left null. Cost-relevant settings that are stated: twist-averaged boundary conditions with 16 x 16 twists for U/t = 8 and 6 (32 x 32 for U/t = 4, 64 x 64 for U/t = 2, in the uniform-phase study); projection time tau t = 1.3 (U/t = 8), 1.73 (U/t = 6), 2.6 (U/t = 4) at the lowest T_eff; a single Trotter step parameter Delta tau optimised. Hardware only as acknowledgements (Marconi/CINECA via PRACE, HOKUSAI/RIKEN). Individual filling/U energies are tabulated in the Supplementary Information, not in the main arXiv text.
